item.content:encoded:
Speaking of scientific fails, I don't really get how it gains energy by turning things into plasma. No matter how you look at it, doing that would only take energy, making this process unsuitable for "feeding". I would understand if that was treated as an anomalous property, but the way its written makes it look like an explanation of a known process, rather than a description of an anomaly.
You can gain energy either by burning (chemical reaction) or through nuclear fusion (in more general terms, to gain energy you need to fuse elements lighter than and split elements heavier than iron, but considering most organic matter is made of light elements, the fox would have to use fusion).
In the case of burning, the energy gained would be actually relatively small. As such, if the fox would really eat this way, we wouldn't see any fire or plasma - instead of wasting the released chemical energy by letting it go into heating up the fuel, the SCP would keep the prey cool, absorbing that energy into itself. Of course, that would constitute a transfer of heat from a cold body to a hot one - a violation of the second law of thermodynamics (more specifically the Clausius statement) - but that seems to be a part of the SCP's anomalous properties, so that's okay. Now that I think about it, this would be a cool anomaly on its own - imagine how strange it would look for things to turn into ash and coal without any flame or change in temperature.
As for fusion, to achieve that you need high temperature and pressure. The fox's surface temperature is already thousands of degrees and is shown to increase rapidly as you get closer, so I assume that's achievable somewhere inside it's body. In this case, I would imagine the fox first killing its prey with heat and then swallowing it inside it's "stomach" for "digestion".

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Well, from the Foundation's point of view, there really isn't anything to be done about it. They can't question it, they can only guess at where it came from and if there are others like it…All they know is that it's a cloud of superheated ionized gas that appears to think it's a fox. The tests are suggesting that it probably wasn't originally a fox, but they have no concrete evidence in either direction. They could try getting a telepath in to read it, but SCPs really aren't supposed to interact…and there's no telling what kind of mind this thing could have. It seems happy enough where it is, it isn't an obvious or overt threat, and if nothing else, it can be used as an incinerator.

Like I said, I wasn't really going for scary with this, and I also didn't want it to be just another 'This thing kills people just for being there' critter. We've got way too many of those, in my opinion. But, if it's not for you, it's not for you. I really don't have a solid picture of what it is myself, but I've put enough hints in the article I think that will tell you what I think. It's a relatively harmless little mystery that the Foundation may never get any real answer to, but at least one researcher has a decent hypothesis going. Completely unconfirmable with even Foundation-level technology, but still a good guess.

If anyone has any ideas of how to expand or improve this, feel free to bring it up here, or over private message, I just ask, as a favor, that you run your ideas past me first and don't just put them live.

It's like with SCP-137. We make it think it's a cat because we-the-Foundation know and understand cat behavior, and a domestic cat is relatively tractable and controllable. Do you really want this thing thinking it's a raccoon or a skunk or, god forbid, a bear?

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
More dangerous does not equal better.

The site is littered with things that kill you because.

To the foundation, this is EITHER: A sapient entity made of superheated plasma akin to that found in a star, that has somehow decided to be a cat, OR: A cat that has become superheated plasma, yet retaining it's feline consciousness.

Now, I don't really have a true backstory for this little guy, but if you're interested, the bits I *do* have are thus:

It wasn't originally a cat. EDIT: That is to say, in-universe, the Plasmacat here was plasma first, and then took on the cat shape.
The 'overfeeding' test was a rather sizable explosion, as it violently expelled the excess mass and energy
The 'cutting' test resulted in another sizable explosion, this time as a defensive mechanism.

There are two reasons I made it a cat. One, yes, the SCPfuel image was the inspiration, though if that was all, I could change it easily. The second reason is more important, and is because of my limitations as a writer. I just don't know enough about the reactions of any other animals to portray normal behaviors in text, which is what this writeup basically requires. It's easy to write yourself stupid, but it's, while probably not impossible, at least very difficult to (convincingly) write yourself more knowledgeable than you really are. If somebody wishes to change it to something besides a cat, and you can keep the writing to at least the standard I set (which is good for me, but probably well below the levels of most veterans here - And though that likely sounds like I'm trying to suck up, that isn't my intention), you're welcome to do so…I'd just like to reserve veto power over your changes, if I may.
